facts.statement: Adratiklit is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Adratiklit (meaning "mountain lizard") is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaur

facts.statement: The genus Adratiklit contains only one known species, Adratiklit boulahfa.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Adratiklit boulahfa.

facts.statement: Adratiklit lived on the supercontinent Gondwana during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the Bathonian age.
facts.quote: lived on the supercontinent Gondwana during the Middle Jurassic (Bathonian age)

facts.statement: Adratiklit is the first described eurypodan dinosaur taxon found in North Africa.
facts.quote: Adratiklit is the first described eurypodan taxon from North Africa

facts.statement: Adratiklit is considered one of the oldest known stegosaurs, alongside Thyreosaurus.
facts.quote: along with Thyreosaurus—one of the oldest known stegosaurs

facts.statement: Adratiklit boulahfa was described by Susannah Maidment, Thomas J. Raven, Driss Ouarhache, and Paul M. Barrett on August 16, 2019.
facts.quote: Adratiklit boulahfa was described by Susannah Maidment, Thomas J. Raven, Driss Ouarhache, and Paul M. Barrett on 16 August 2019

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Adratiklit boulahfa is a single dorsal vertebra cataloged as NHMUK PV R37366.
facts.quote: The holotype of Adratiklit boulahfa is a dorsal vertebra, NHMUK PV R37366

facts.statement: The fossils of Adratiklit were acquired by the Natural History Museum in the United Kingdom from fossil traders.
facts.quote: The specimens were acquired by the Natural History Museum in the United Kingdom from fossil traders

facts.statement: The known specimens of Adratiklit represent multiple individuals, estimated to be around five.
facts.quote: They represent multiple individuals, probably five

facts.statement: The fossilized humerus of Adratiklit measures 61 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The fossilized humerus is 61 cm long

facts.statement: The unique skeletal traits identified in Adratiklit are diagnostic for the entire Stegosauria group.
facts.quote: These traits are unique for the Stegosauria as a whole and are diagnostic to this taxon

facts.statement: Adratiklit is classified within the subfamily Dacentrurinae, being more closely related to European stegosaurs like Dacentrurus and Miragaia than to southern African taxa.
facts.quote: Maidment et al. (2020) identified Adratiklit as more closely related to the European stegosaurs Dacentrurus and Miragaia in the subfamily Dacentrurinae

facts.statement: Adratiklit belongs to the family Stegosauridae.
Adratiklit lived during the middle Jurassic period, approximately between 168 and 166 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 168 a 166 millones de años

facts.statement: Adratiklit lived in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy África

facts.statement: Remains of Adratiklit were found in the El Mers Group, likely the El Mers II Formation, near Boulahfa, south of Boulemane in Fès-Meknes, Morocco.
facts.quote: Sus restos fueron encontrados en el Grupo El Mers, probablemente en la Formación El Mers II, cerca de Boulahfa, al sur de Boulemane, Fès-Meknes, Marruecos

facts.statement: Adratiklit is the first eurypodan taxon from North Africa and the oldest definitive stegosaur found anywhere in the world.
facts.quote: Adratiklit es el primer taxón eurípodo del norte de África y el estegosáurido definitivo más antiguo de cualquier parte del mundo

facts.statement: Adratiklit lived from the Bathonian to the Callovian stages, between 168.2 and 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Callovian (168.2 to 161.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Adratiklit had an estimated body length of up to 7 meters.
rejected.quote: Adratiklit has an estimated body length of up to 7 m
